title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
subtitle: crispy pan-fried chicken with pineapple, onion and carrot in a glossy sweet-tangy sauce, over rice
imageAlt: Crispy chicken pieces with pineapple chunks in a glossy red-orange sauce beside rice in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Ketchup, rice vinegar, brown sugar, soy

beforeYouStart.text: Drain the pineapple over a bowl: you need ½ cup of the juice for the sauce.

items.name: pineapple chunks in juice
items.note: 398 ml, drained, ½ cup juice saved

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Whisk ½ cup of the saved pineapple juice with the ketchup, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce and the cornstarch mixed with water.

steps.title: Coat the chicken
steps.text: Season the chicken with the salt and toss in the egg. Mix the cornstarch and flour, then toss the chicken in it until fully coated, shaking off the extra.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Fry the chicken in 2 batches, 5–6 minutes, turning, until golden, crisp and 74°C (165°F). Drain on a rack.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the onion and carrot 3 minutes, then the garlic 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Add the pineapple chunks, stir the sauce and pour it in. Simmer 1–2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Toss the chicken in the sauce and serve right away over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Toss in the sauce at the very last second and serve right away.
Stir in a splash of water or pineapple juice.
Add 1 tbsp more brown sugar; vinegars vary.

saleTip: Canned pineapple is often under $1.50 at No Frills; keep a few cans in the pantry.
swap: Air fryer: coat the chicken, spray with oil and air-fry at 200°C (400°F) 10–12 minutes, shaking halfway, to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: The coating softens but the flavour is great; reheat covered in the microwave.
doneness: 74°C (165°F) in the largest piece (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested sweet and sour chicken methods (Canadian Living, Woks of Life): cornstarch-coated chicken pan-fried crisp, tossed in a pineapple juice, ketchup and vinegar sauce thickened with cornstarch.
prepAhead: Mix the sauce and cut the vegetables up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F), or in the air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 5 minutes to re-crisp the chicken.

basic.note: Chicken and pineapple in the sauce, no vegetables.

fancy.note: Toasted sesame and a splash of sesame oil in the sauce.

stepNotes.5: Fancy: stir the sesame oil into the sauce at the end.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Scatter the sesame seeds over each bowl.

plating: Rice packed into a bowl and turned out.

why.1-3: A cornstarch-heavy coating fries up lighter and crunchier than flour alone.
why.0-2: Rice vinegar gives the sour without being harsh.

funFact: Sweet and sour pork from Guangdong is the ancestor; the bright red ketchup version is a North American Chinese restaurant creation.
pairs: lo mein on the side for a takeout night
